title: Approval publication rejects legacy evidence that could never merge with approval

consumerGuidance.architecture: MARC's trusted controller is Node.js CommonJS with no runtime dependencies. Legacy SHA-named report evidence without reportCreatedAt remains unchanged and verifiable; never rename history. Operator approval may be supplied to merge after the report pair is published.
consumerGuidance.notes: Reduced from PR16 to the two controller files that own approval publication; the other PR16 files do not affect this behavior.

forbiddenFindings.example: Claiming the reportCreatedAt guard at marc.cjs:549 removes an approval-merge path for legacy SHA-named reports; the base required a matching humanApprovalAudit, which no legacy report can carry, so that state never merged with approval.
Reporting the documented non-atomic GitHub description update in record-approval as a defect, or asking for a different receipt hash algorithm.
Returning repair or human-required for this seam as if the legacy guard were a defect or an open business decision.

notes: False-alarm probe from PR16. Three fresh reviewers and the first adjudication flagged a legacy-report regression here; source history refutes it (see rubric). Version 3 reclassifies the earlier seeded-defect versions. Other PR16 defects are outside this reduced case.
